\begin{frame}{What is a Circle Packing?}

\begin{columns}


\column{6.75cm}

\includegraphics[width=6.75cm]{unca_pics/0_owl1}<1|handout:0>\includegraphics[width=6.75cm]{unca_pics/0_owl2}<2|handout:0>\includegraphics[width=6.75cm]{unca_pics/0_owl3}<3|handout:0>\includegraphics[width=6.75cm]{unca_pics/0_owl4}<4>

\column{5.0cm}
\begin{block}{A collection of circles with a pattern such that}

\begin{enumerate}
\item [1.]<2->The circles have one and only one circle, $C_{i}$, associated
with each vertex $v_{i}$ in the pattern.
\item [2.]<3->Any two neighbors in the circle collection are \emph{tangent.}
\item [3.]<4->$\{C_{i},C_{j},C_{k}\}$ form a positively oriented triple
whenever $\{v_{i},v_{j},v_{k}\}$ form a positively oriented face
in the pattern.
\end{enumerate}
\end{block}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Preliminaries for KAT Proof}

\begin{columns}


\column{6cm}

\vfill
\begin{block}{Monotonicity\emph{Given a face of circles at $v_{i}$, $v_{j}$, and
$v_{k}$ in $\mathbb{C}$ or $\mathbb{D}$. }}

\begin{itemize}
\item []\emph{The angle at $v_{i}$ is }\emph{\uline{strictly and continuously
}}\uline{decreasing}\emph{ wrt to the radius at $v_{i}$.}
\item []\emph{The angles at $v_{j}$ and $v_{k}$ are }\emph{\uline{strictly
and continuously }}\uline{increasing} \emph{wrt to the radius at $v_{i}$.}
\end{itemize}
\end{block}
\vfill

\column{5.5cm}

\begin{frame}{KAT Proof}

\begin{itemize}
\item []<2->Let $r_{i}$ be the radius at $v_{i}$. Define a \textbf{radii
assignment function},\textbf{\emph{ $\mathfrak{R}$}}\emph{
\[
\mathfrak{R}(r_{i})=\begin{cases}
\mbox{set \ensuremath{r_{i}}so the angle sum at \ensuremath{v_{i}}is \ensuremath{2\pi}} & \mbox{if }v_{i}\in\mbox{interior}\\
\mbox{unchanged} & \mbox{if }v_{i}\in\mbox{boundary}
\end{cases}
\]
}\vspace{-.5cm}
\end{itemize}

\begin{frame}{KAT Proof}

\begin{itemize}
\item []<1->Let $r_{i}$ be the radius at $v_{i}$. Define a \textbf{radii
assignment function},\textbf{\emph{ $\mathfrak{R}$}}\emph{
\[
\mathfrak{R}(r_{i})=\begin{cases}
\mbox{set \ensuremath{r_{i}}so the angle sum at \ensuremath{v_{i}}is \ensuremath{2\pi}} & \mbox{if }v_{i}\in\mbox{interior}\\
\mbox{unchanged} & \mbox{if }v_{i}\in\mbox{boundary}
\end{cases}
\]
}\vspace{-.75cm}

\begin{columns}


\column{5cm}
\begin{itemize}
\item Start in $\mathbb{C}$ or $\mathbb{D}$, so we have

\begin{itemize}
\item Border circles
\item Monotonicity
\end{itemize}
\end{itemize}
\begin{block}<2->{Lemma}
 Given two radii collection for a pattern, such that $R'\leq R$
then $\mathfrak{R}(R')\leq\mathfrak{R}(R)$.
\end{block}

\column{7cm}
\begin{itemize}
\item [] \uncover<3->{\includegraphics[width=3cm]{unca_pics/6_flower1}}\uncover<5->{\includegraphics[width=3cm]{unca_pics/6_flower2}}
\item [] \vspace{-.3cm} \uncover<4->{\includegraphics[width=3cm]{unca_pics/6_flower3}}\uncover<6->{\includegraphics[width=3cm]{unca_pics/6_flower4}}
\end{itemize}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{KAT Proof}

\begin{itemize}
\item []<1->Let $r_{i}$ be the radius at $v_{i}$. Define a \textbf{radii
assignment function},\textbf{\emph{ $\mathfrak{R}$}}\emph{
\[
\mathfrak{R}(r_{i})=\begin{cases}
\mbox{set \ensuremath{r_{i}}so the angle sum at \ensuremath{v_{i}}is \ensuremath{2\pi}} & \mbox{if }v_{i}\in\mbox{interior}\\
\mbox{unchanged} & \mbox{if }v_{i}\in\mbox{boundary}
\end{cases}
\]
}\vspace{-.75cm}
\end{itemize}
\begin{columns}


\column{12cm}
\begin{block}<1->{Lemma}
 Given two radii collection for a pattern, such that $R'\leq R$
then $\mathfrak{R}(R')\leq\mathfrak{R}(R)$.
\end{block}
\begin{itemize}
\item []<2->So $\mathfrak{R}(R)\leq R\iff\mathfrak{R}^{k+1}(R')\leq\mathfrak{R}^{k}(R)$
\item []<3->and \textrm{$\mathfrak{R}(R)\leq R\iff$angle sums of $R\leq2\pi$.}
\item []<4->and \textrm{$\mathfrak{R}^{k+1}(R)\leq\mathfrak{R}^{k}(R)\iff$angle
sums of $\mathfrak{R}^{k}(R)\leq2\pi$.}
\end{itemize}
\end{columns}
\begin{itemize}
\item <5->Now choose some really big radii; so that $\mathfrak{R}(R_{\infty})<R_{\infty}$,
and it converges.
\item <6->$\dots$with some details. 
\end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{KAT Proof}

\begin{columns}


\column{5.5cm}
\begin{block}{Theorem}
\emph{ There exists a unique CP for any simply connected pattern
with a collection of border circles in $\mathbb{C}$ or $\mathbb{D}$.}
\end{block}
\begin{itemize}
\item <2->Maximality argument$\Rightarrow$uniqueness.
\item <3->To get on the sphere$\dots$
\end{itemize}
\begin{block}<8->{Koebe-Andreev-Thurston Theorem (KAT)}
 \emph{There exists a CP on the sphere for any finite triangulation
of the sphere. Furthermore, this CP is unique up to Möbius transformations.} 
\end{block}

\column{5.5cm}

\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Riemann Mapping Theorem}

\only<1-1>{
\begin{block}{Classical RMT}
\emph{If $R$ is a non-empty simply connected proper subset of $\mathbb{C}$,
then there exists an essentially unique mapping from $R$ onto the
unit disc. }
\end{block}
}

\only<2->{
\begin{block}{Discrete RMT}
\emph{If $C$ is a simply connected finite circle packing in $\mathbb{C}$,
then there exists an essentially unique maximal packing of with the
same pattern in $\mathbb{D}$. }
\end{block}
}

\only<1>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/1_RMT1a}}\only<2>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/1_RMT2}}\only<3>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/1_RMT3}}\only<4>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/1_RMT4}}\only<5>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/1_RMT5}}\only<6>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/1_RMT6}}\only<7>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/1_RMT8}}\only<8>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/1_RMT10}}\only<9>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/1_RMT12}}\only<10>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/1_RMT14}}\only<11>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/1_RMT15}}\only<12>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/2_R1}}\only<13>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/2_R2}}\only<14>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/2_R3}}\only<15>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/2_R6}}\only<16>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/2_R9}}\only<17>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/2_R12}}\only<18>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/2_R14}}\only<19>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/3R1}}\only<20>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/3R2}}\only<21>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/3R3}}\only<22>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/3R4}}\only<23>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/3R5}}\only<24>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/3R7}}\only<25>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/3R9}}\only<26>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/3R12}}\only<27>{\includegraphics[width=11cm]{unca_pics/RMT/1_RMT1a}}

\begin{frame}{Fractional Branching}

\begin{columns}


\column{6cm}

Choose an interior face $f=\{v_{1},v_{2},v_{3}\}$. Is there a way
to split the extra angle amongst the vertices to get a branched packing? 
\begin{block}<4->{Theorem}

$\iff$the extra angle at $v_{i}$ is $2(\angle v_{i}v_{j}$$v_{k})$
for $v_{i},v_{j},v_{k}\in f$.
\end{block}

\begin{block}<11->{Theorem}

If the pattern is simply connected then there (usually) exists a fractional
branching on very interior face\textbf{.}
\end{block}
\begin{itemize}
\item <12->Proof using Brouwer fixed point theorem. 
\end{itemize}

\column{5cm}

\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Thomson Problem}

\begin{columns}


\column{6cm}

How to find the min. energy distribution of $N$ electrons on the
surface of a sphere?
\[
E=\sum_{i<j}\frac{1}{\left|p_{i}-p_{j}\right|}
\]

\begin{itemize}
\item <2-> A CP exists for any triangulation.
\item <3-> The CP can be computed by \href{http://www.math.utk.edu/~kens/CirclePack/}{\textcolor{blue}{\tt{CirclePack}}}.
\item <4-> As $N\rightarrow\infty$, a CP analogue will converge towards
its continuous counterpart.
\end{itemize}
\begin{exampleblock}<4->{}

\begin{itemize}
\item <5->[1.] Triangulate existing data pts.
\item <6->[2.] Compute using \tt{CirclePack}.
\item <7->[3.] Normalize the packing.
\end{itemize}
\end{exampleblock}
